name: TILE-1-the-tile-steals-a-class-another-module-already-draws
note: This is not hypothetical: `.tile` IS the inventory and trade item icon (30x30), and the first cut of the save tile used it. Every tile drew at 34x34 and every measurement in the probe was about a rule written for something else. A later CSS rule wins, silently.

name: TILE-2-the-portrait-blocks-the-list
note: The well is empty for as long as the CIF takes, so a pane of ten saves opens as ten empty boxes - and a face that never loads leaves them empty for ever. The initial is what makes a slow or missing portrait an ordinary tile.

name: TILE-3-a-face-that-will-not-load-escapes-into-the-pane
note: An unhandled rejection out of a menu repaint, on every player whose copy of Daggerfall has no FACE CIF. The chargen wizard's own law is NEVER TRAPS, on a surface a player reaches far more often.

name: TILE-4-a-disabled-button-is-still-wired
note: The Load button is disabled in the pause pane where the host has no quickLoad. A handler behind a disabled button is a press that does something on a keyboard, and the pane disabled it because it CANNOT be done.

name: TILE-5-no-account-is-nagged-on-every-tile
note: ACC0's wall is at cloud saves and a player who has not asked for an account is not told about it on every tile they own. `off` is the state most players are in.

name: TILE-6-a-refusal-gets-a-second-sentence-here
note: The service says WHY - full backup, too large, signed out - and accountClient.js owns the sentence for each. Dropping it here throws the only useful half away and leaves a player with nothing to act on.

name: TILE-7-a-clock-that-ran-backwards-is-a-negative-age
note: A clock that ran backwards. The service's stamp and the browser's clock are two clocks and they disagree - but the FIRST branch already answers this, so the clamp changes nothing that can be observed.
why: EQUIVALENT, and recorded rather than pinned around. A negative age is always under the 90-second threshold, so it answers 'just now' either way - the clamp is belt for a reader, not a branch. Driven to find that out: the pin that presents a stamp from the future passes with the clamp gone.

name: TILE-8-the-singular-goes-back-to-being-unreachable
note: Past the 90-second threshold `Math.round(d / 60)` is never 1, so "1 minute ago" is a branch nothing can produce - found by writing the pin rather than by reading the code.

name: TILE-9-the-save-envelope-s-identity-is-thrown-away-again
note: S3c/U9 put race, gender and faceIndex on the envelope years of slices ago; the menu's row simply never read them. Without the face index every tile draws face 0 - the wrong character, confidently.

name: TILE-10-the-face-goes-back-to-living-inside-the-wizard
note: The one home, unplugged from its first caller: the wizard silently loses every portrait while the tile keeps its own, which is exactly the drift two copies produce and the reason it moved.

name: TILE-11-one-pane-keeps-its-own-card
note: Three panes list the same slots. Leaving one of them drawing something else is how three panes come to disagree about what a save is, which is the whole reason one tile exists.
